policy_title: Halve Knife Crime and Establish Young Futures Hubs
stated: Labour aims to halve knife crime in a decade by ensuring knife carrying triggers rapid intervention and tough consequences, including mandatory prevention plans, curfews, tagging, or custody for young offenders. They will ban ninja swords, zombie-style blades, and machetes, and strengthen rules to prevent online sales with personal accountability for executives. A new Young Futures programme with hubs across communities will provide youth workers, mental health support, and careers advice, alongside youth workers in A&E units and Pupil Referral Units. A new offence of criminal exploitation of children will target gangs.

source.quote: The next Labour government will change this. We aim to halve knife crime in a decade. Labour will end the practice of empty warnings by ensuring knife carrying triggers rapid intervention and tough consequences. Every young person caught in possession of a knife will be referred to a Youth Offending Team and will receive a mandatory plan to prevent reoffending, with penalties including curfews, tagging, and custody for the most serious cases. To get knives off our streets Labour will ban ninja swords, lethal zombie-style blades and machetes, and strengthen rules to prevent online sales. Executives of online companies that flout these rules will be personally held to account through tough sanctions. Labour will intervene earlier to stop young people being drawn into crime, creating a new Young Futures programme with a network of hubs reaching every community. These hubs will have youth workers, mental health support workers, and careers advisers on hand to support young people’s mental health and avoid them being drawn into crime. And to offer young people a pathway out of violence, we will place youth workers and mentors in A&E units and Pupil Referral Units, funded by full recovery of the cost of firearm licensing. Labour will also introduce a new offence of criminal exploitation of children, to go after the gangs who are luring young people into violence and crime.

bearing_set.reason: The policy directly targets knife crime rates, introduces criminal justice consequences (curfews, tagging, custody, mandatory plans), bans specific weapon types, tightens supply-chain enforcement, and creates a new gang-exploitation offence — all core safety and justice indicators.

Young Futures Hubs provide careers advice and skills support to at-risk youth, and youth workers are placed specifically in Pupil Referral Units — both mechanisms plausibly move the attainment gap and skills/opportunity indicators for the most excluded young people.

Mandatory curfews, electronic tagging, and compulsory prevention plans for young offenders are concrete state coercive/surveillance powers that restrict freedom of movement and impose conditions without full criminal conviction — a non-negligible liberty cost with a specific mechanism.

membership_note: Three genuine bearings: O5 (the policy's designed-for safety effect), O10 (the liberty cost of mandatory coercive interventions), and O7 (the opportunity/skills-access effect through hubs and PRU presence). Mental health support in hubs is noted but routes primarily through O5 prevention rather than O3 (healthcare access/capacity). Community cohesion effects are plausible but not mechanistically specific enough to clear the non-negligible bar for O15.
